construction_markdown:
No leaderboard construction is claimed.

Start from Bouyukliev’s published binary [68,8,32] code G₁ and delete the left-to-right, 1-based coordinates P={1,2,3,9,14}. Equivalently, define J as the row span over F₂ of the following self-contained 8×63 matrix:

```text
000000000000000000000001111111111111111111111111111111111111111
000001111111111111111110000000000000000000011111111111111111111
111110000111111111111110000000000111111111100000000001111111111
001111111000000011111110000011111000111111100000111110001111111
111110001000111100000110111100011011000111100111001111110000111
110111110011011100111110001101111100001001101011000010110111001
011010111111100101011111010110011101010010001001010100010011111
101001010101101110101011011110101110000110101011011001110101011
```

Thus J={uG:u∈F₂⁸}. If an alphabet identification is desired, fix F₂₅₆=F₂[a]/(a⁸+a⁴+a³+a+1), use the coefficient basis 1,a,…,a⁷, and encode the symbol Σuᵣaʳ as uG.

The puncture set is also characterized without hidden choice: it is the lexicographically first five-subset of the 68 coordinates that is not contained in the support of any weight-32 word of G₁. The construction itself uses the displayed literal set, so no search or external database is needed to recover it.
distance_audit: Exact enumeration of all 256 row combinations gives one zero word and minimum nonzero weight 28; hence the constituent is exactly [63,8,28]₂.

MacWilliams evaluation was performed through both the binomial Krawtchouk formula and its three-term recurrence. Both give dual dimension 55, dual distance 3, and identical coefficients in every shell.
For all 1≤i≤63, A_i(J⊥)≤C(63,i)/217. Equality occurs only at i=61, where A_61(J⊥)=9 and C(63,61)=1953.

No distance claim is made for a length-2^30 code. The product-distance calculation is explicitly only a certificate bound and is not inverted into an upper bound on actual symbol-sensitive concatenated distance.
explicitness_audit: The binary generator, coordinate ordering, puncture set, and optional F₂₅₆ identification are literal and deterministic.
All 256 inner messages and all 63 dual shells are finite symbolically specified computations; no random sampling is used.
The puncture was independently recomputed from the published G₁ matrix, and the spectrum and MacWilliams audit were independently recomputed by separate agents.
No outer code satisfying the Doron–Mosheiff–Wootters product-distribution condition is asserted.
No tower, divisor, graph, shortening, repetition, or padding is hidden in this non-leaderboard result.
The workspace was read-only, so the proof was returned here rather than written into proofs/ or data/records.json.

next_tasks: Seek a scalable algebraic family whose dual satisfies every DMW shell bound; direct sums of the present constituent fail beginning with four copies.
Replace the published n₀≥64/ρ⁴ argument with a genuinely finite small-inner analysis tailored to an explicitly enumerated constituent such as J.
Construct and prove an explicit outer code satisfying DMW Equation (11); the paper only establishes existence by averaging over random outer codes.
For a record-rate DMW instantiation, reduce the effective distance constant from at least 288 ln 2≈199.626 to at most 2.1327407, while also eliminating the unquantified sufficiently-large threshold.
Investigate BCH-dual or deterministic-puncturing candidates using exact all-shell enumerators rather than only minimum distance, bias, or bounded-local properties.
When write access is available, place this lemma and proof in proofs/ and add it as a research/proof-tool entry in data/records.json.
obstructions: Every even-weight binary inner code C fails DMW τ-niceness for every 0<τ<rate(C): the all-one vector lies in C⊥, and the i=n shell would require 1≤2^{-n(rate−τ)}<1. This excludes both the unpunctured G₁ and RM(1,7).
For J, Theorem 5.1 would require n₀≥ceil(64/(8/63)^4)=246,141, whereas J has n₀=63.
Direct sums do not repair the size failure: J^⊕t has A_3((J^⊕t)⊥)=109t and fails τ=1/sqrt(63t) niceness for every t≥4.
Using only the ordinary minimum-distance product certificate, J forces outer distance at least 2^24; Singleton then caps the binary dimension at 2,130,448, below the current 3,688,448.
With the constants explicitly admitted by the published DMW proof, target distance forces ρ≤1/(2304 ln 2), which gives at most 421 binary dimensions and requires an inner block longer than 2^30.

DMW Theorem 5.1 additionally needs an explicit outer satisfying its product-distribution condition. The cited paper proves existence through a random outer code and presents explicit construction as future work.

Integrality of the niceness inequality forces A_i(C⊥)=0 whenever log₂ C(n,i)<ρn−sqrt(n). A scalable constant-rate nice family must therefore give a near-GV dual-distance certificate together with bounds in every shell, substantially more than small bias or ordinary minimum distance.

proof_markdown:
### Proposition 1: exact deterministic inner code

Let G be the displayed 8×63 matrix and J={uG:u∈F₂⁸}. The mother matrix is the G₁ printed by [Bouyukliev](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2008.12.002), punctured at P={1,2,3,9,14}.

The following finite symbolic sum computes the enumerator without sampling:

`W_J(z)=Σ_{u∈F₂⁸} z^{Σ_{j=1}^{63} ((Σ_{r=1}^{8}u_r G_{rj}) mod 2)}`.

Exact XOR evaluation gives

`W_J(z)=1+28z^28+66z^29+50z^30+30z^31+13z^32+20z^36+30z^37+14z^38+2z^39+2z^40`.

As a second certificate, the 187 weight-32 mother words meet P in 0,1,2,3,4,5 positions with multiplicities 13,30,50,66,28,0; the 68 weight-40 words give 2,2,14,30,20,0. These numbers produce the same polynomial after puncturing. Its constant coefficient is one even though all 256 messages were evaluated, so the kernel of u↦uG is trivial and rank(G)=8. Its least positive exponent is 28. Therefore J is exactly [63,8,28]₂.

### Proposition 2: exact DMW niceness threshold

Write A_w for the coefficients above and B_i=A_i(J⊥). Character orthogonality gives the MacWilliams shell formula

`B_i=2^{-8} Σ_w A_w K_i(w)`,

where

`K_i(w)=Σ_j (−1)^j C(w,j)C(63−w,i−j)`.

For direct reconstruction one may instead use

`K_0(w)=1`, `K_1(w)=63−2w`,

`(r+1)K_{r+1}(w)=(63−2w)K_r(w)−(64−r)K_{r−1}(w)`.

Exact integer evaluation gives B_1=B_2=0, B_3=109, B_61=9, B_62=B_63=0, Σ_iB_i=2^55, and the following grouped maxima. The last column is the maximum of 128B_i/C(63,i) over the indicated shells.

| shells | maximizing i | exact maximum |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1–10 | 5 | 2944/5673 |
| 11–20 | 13 | 5234347504000/10468434365991 |
| 21–30 | 22 | 163751599871488/327503186589285 |
| 31–40 | 38 | 4213498052290048/8426995787342223 |
| 41–50 | 48 | 20355320083072/40710578089965 |
| 51–60 | 60 | 6784/13237 |
| 61–63 | 61 | 128/217 |

Thus the global maximum is 128/217, uniquely at i=61. Equivalently,

`B_i≤C(63,i)/217` for every 1≤i≤63.

For rate ρ=8/63, DMW Definition 2.2 asks for

`B_i≤C(63,i)·2^{-63(ρ−τ)}=C(63,i)·2^{-8+63τ}`.

Consequently the exact least admissible τ is

`τ*=(8−log₂217)/63≈0.00378490107231`.

In particular τ=1/63 works because its right side is C(63,i)/128. Niceness is monotone in τ, and

`1/63 < 1/sqrt(63) < 8/63`,

so J satisfies precisely the inner niceness hypothesis τ=1/sqrt(n₀) used in [DMW Theorem 5.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.08584v3).

### Lemma 3: endpoint obstruction for even-weight inners

Let C be an even-weight binary [n,k] code of rate ρ. Then the all-one vector belongs to C⊥, so A_n(C⊥)≥1. For every 0<τ<ρ, niceness at shell i=n would require

`1≤A_n(C⊥)≤C(n,n)2^{-n(ρ−τ)}<1`,

a contradiction. Thus puncturing away the endpoint obstruction is necessary for the even-weight G₁ and for RM(1,7).

### Lemma 4: fixed-block repetition does not scale niceness

The dual of J has minimum distance 3 and B_3=109. Hence

`A_3((J^⊕t)⊥)=109t`.

At rate 8/63 and τ=1/sqrt(63t), the required upper bound is

`R_t=C(63t,3)2^{-8t+sqrt(63t)}`.

Already at t=4, R_4≈36.86<436. The failure persists: using C(63t,3)<(63t)^3/6, the upper bound for R_t/t is a constant times `t²2^{-8t+sqrt(63t)}`. For t≥4, its successive ratio is less than

`(5/4)²·2^{-8+2}<1`,

because sqrt(63(t+1))−sqrt(63t)<2. Therefore R_t/t decreases for t≥4 and remains below 109. Thus J^⊕t is not DMW-nice for any t≥4. In particular, direct sum cannot reach the 246,141-coordinate size hypothesis.

### Lemma 5: ordinary product-distance use is below the record

At most

`M=floor(2^30/63)=17,043,521`

inner blocks fit, leaving one zero coordinate. If distance is certified solely by `d_binary≥28d_out`, the target forces

`d_out≥ceil(469,762,048/28)=16,777,216`.

Singleton, proved by puncturing d_out−1 coordinates injectively, gives at most M−d_out+1=266,306 F₂₅₆ symbols of information, or

`8·266,306=2,130,448`

binary dimensions. This is below 3,688,448. This lemma is deliberately scoped to the minimum-distance product certificate: a symbol-value-sensitive proof could exploit the nonconstant inner weights and is not excluded.

### Proposition 6: the published DMW finite certificate cannot fit N=2^30

DMW Theorem 5.1 gives rate ρ² and relative distance at least `(1−cρ)/2`. Claim 5.4 and its proof explicitly admit constants satisfying

`c̃≥4 ln 2`, `c≥72c̃`.

Taking their smallest displayed choices gives c=288 ln 2. Any direct output of raw length at most N, including one subsequently zero-padded to N, can certify the target only if

`(1−cρ)/2≥7/16`,

so

`ρ≤1/(8c)=1/(2304 ln 2)`.

It follows that its integer binary dimension is at most

`floor(Nρ²)≤floor(2^30/(2304 ln 2)²)=421`.

Moreover, the theorem requires

`n₀≥64/ρ⁴≥64(2304 ln 2)^4`,

whose integer lower bound is 416,305,086,453,856, larger than the entire target length. Thus even one inner block cannot fit. These are obstructions to a direct finite use of the constants exposed by the published proof, not lower bounds on every possible refinement of the DMW method.

Finally, Theorem 5.1 also assumes an outer code satisfying its Equation (11). The paper establishes existence by averaging over a random outer code and explicitly leaves construction of such an outer code as a goal. Hence the deterministic inner J removes one small randomness issue but does not yield a deterministic target code.

Therefore this is a proved constituent and obstruction result, with no leaderboard submission and no claim to beat 7/1920.

proof_steps.statement: J deterministically satisfies the randomized-inner niceness property required by DMW at length 63.

proof_steps.statement: Even-weight constituents and fixed direct-sum scaling cannot supply the required scalable nice family.

proof_steps.proof: There are 17,043,521 inner slots and product distance requires outer distance 2^24. Singleton yields at most 266,306 alphabet dimensions, hence 2,130,448 binary dimensions.

research_direction: The certified [63,8,28] constituent proves that deterministic DMW-nice inner codes exist at small finite length once the even-weight endpoint is punctured. The real bottleneck is scalable all-shell niceness together with a much sharper finite concatenation analysis and an explicit outer code satisfying the DMW product-distribution condition.
theorem_statement: Let J be the row span of the displayed matrix obtained by deleting coordinates {1,2,3,9,14} from Bouyukliev’s G₁. Then J is a deterministic [63,8,28]₂ code with exact weight enumerator 1+28z^28+66z^29+50z^30+30z^31+13z^32+20z^36+30z^37+14z^38+2z^39+2z^40. For every 1≤i≤63, A_i(J⊥)≤C(63,i)/217, with equality only at i=61. Hence its exact DMW niceness threshold is τ*=(8−log₂217)/63, and in particular it is 1/sqrt(63)-nice. Nevertheless, direct sums cease to be nice from four copies onward; ordinary product-distance concatenation has binary Singleton cap 2,130,448; and the constants exposed by the published DMW Theorem 5.1 proof force inner length greater than 2^30 and final dimension at most 421 at relative distance 7/16. Thus the constituent is a proved deterministic proof tool, not a target-length construction.
title: A deterministic DMW-nice [63,8,28] inner code and finite-length obstruction
